bull.t: Recurring SaaS Growth And Cash Generation
bull.b: Strong recurring and SaaS revenue growth supports durable visibility because Tyler’s government software relationships generate repeatable demand. Record free cash flow and expanding margins further indicate that growth is converting into internally funded financial capacity.

The large installed base and active customer engagement create a multi-year migration pathway from on-premise systems to Tyler’s cloud platform. Cloud conversion can deepen customer integration, support recurring revenue growth, and improve delivery efficiency through a common code stream.

Embedding payments into core government workflows broadens Tyler’s revenue streams while increasing the value of its existing software relationships. Cross-selling within the installed base can strengthen customer retention and produce additional usage-linked revenue without requiring entirely new accounts.

bear.b: The sharp increase in debt relative to equity reduces balance-sheet flexibility compared with prior years. Higher leverage can constrain future acquisition, investment, and shareholder-return choices, while making the company more sensitive to weaker operating results or changes in financing conditions.

SaaS growth below the long-term target could moderate the pace at which Tyler expands its recurring revenue base. Although demand remains healthy, sustained deceleration would make the 2030 objectives more dependent on successful cloud flips, acquisitions, and improved execution.

bear.t: Shorter Contracts And Uneven AI Adoption
bear.b: Shorter contract duration may reduce revenue visibility and increase renewal exposure, while uneven AI adoption limits near-term monetization of new capabilities. Tyler must demonstrate measurable returns and predictable pricing before these products become a broad, durable growth contributor.
